source_refs.note: Exercise 3.5, Question 4 (i), (ii): simplify with Properties II-IV; book p. 101. Key on p. 300 under 'Exercise 3.2'; key for (ii) fits a '+' third integral.

blocks.explanation:
No formula for \(f\) is given, so we can only combine the integrals with the properties.
Use Property II to turn 'minus with reversed limits' into a forward integral, then Property III to join neighbouring intervals.
Aim: one integral, or zero.
steps:
Given: \(E = \int_{0}^{1} f - \int_{0}^{2} f - \int_{3}^{1} f + \int_{3}^{2} f\) (all with \(dx\)).
To find: the simplest form of \(E\).
Method: Property II \(\int_a^b f = -\int_b^a f\) and Property III \(\int_a^c f + \int_c^b f = \int_a^b f\).

Reverse the limits
\[-\int_{3}^{1} f(x)\,dx = \int_{1}^{3} f(x)\,dx\]
\[\int_{3}^{2} f(x)\,dx = -\int_{2}^{3} f(x)\,dx\]
Why: Property II: swapping the limits changes the sign.

Regroup
\[E = \left(\int_{0}^{1} f + \int_{1}^{3} f\right) - \left(\int_{0}^{2} f + \int_{2}^{3} f\right)\]
Why: put the plus terms together and the minus terms together.

Join the intervals
\[E = \int_{0}^{3} f(x)\,dx - \int_{0}^{3} f(x)\,dx = 0\]
Why: Property III: \([0, 1] \cup [1, 3] = [0, 3]\) and \([0, 2] \cup [2, 3] = [0, 3]\).

Check with \(f(x) = 1\)
\[1 - 2 - (-2) + (-1) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: for \(f = 1\) each integral is (upper limit minus lower limit). The key prints 0.

blocks.explanation:
Again no formula for \(f\): simplify with the properties.
First remove \(f(4 - x)\) and \(f(5 - x)\) with Property IV (their limits add up to 4 and 5), then take out the constants and combine intervals.
Watch every sign as printed.
steps:
Given: \(E = 5\int_{0}^{3} f(x)\,dx - 5\int_{1}^{3} f(4 - x)\,dx - 5\int_{1}^{5} f(x)\,dx - 4\int_{0}^{5} f(5 - x)\,dx\).
To find: the simplest form of \(E\).
Method: Property IX (constants come out), Property IV \(\int_a^b f(a + b - x)\,dx = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx\), Property III.

Rewrite \(E\)
\[E = 5\int_{0}^{3} f - 5\int_{1}^{3} f - 5\int_{1}^{5} f - 4\int_{0}^{5} f\]
Why: substitute the two results (every integral is now of \(f(x)\,dx\)).

Combine the first two
\[5\int_{0}^{3} f - 5\int_{1}^{3} f = 5\int_{0}^{1} f\]
Why: Property III: \(\int_0^3 f = \int_0^1 f + \int_1^3 f\).

Split the last one and collect
\[4\int_{0}^{5} f = 4\int_{0}^{1} f + 4\int_{1}^{5} f\]
\[E = 5\int_{0}^{1} f - 5\int_{1}^{5} f - 4\int_{0}^{1} f - 4\int_{1}^{5} f\]
\[E = \int_{0}^{1} f(x)\,dx - 9\int_{1}^{5} f(x)\,dx\]
Why: Property III, then collect like integrals: \(5 - 4 = 1\) and \(-5 - 4 = -9\). This cannot be joined further.

Check with \(f(x) = 1\)
\[5(3) - 5(2) - 5(4) - 4(5) = -35\]
\[1 - 9(4) = -35 \;\checkmark\]
Why: for \(f = 1\) every integral equals the length of its interval; both forms agree.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(\int_{0}^{5} f(x)\,dx\). That is the result only if the third integral is added, i.e. \(\ldots + \int_{1}^{5} 5f(x)\,dx \ldots\): then \(E = 5\int_0^1 f + 5\int_1^5 f - 4\int_0^5 f = \int_0^5 f\). With the signs as printed the result is \(\int_{0}^{1} f(x)\,dx - 9\int_{1}^{5} f(x)\,dx\) (test \(f = 1\): \(-35\), not 5). Either the key or the sign before the third integral is a misprint.
